text:
Mats Zuccarello is 39, in his first season with Los Angeles after 452 games in Minnesota, and the story so far is mostly about time missed. He played six games in October, went on injured reserve, and came back on Nov. 10. Nine games in, he has a goal and an assist, both on the power play, and the Kings have lost the three games since his return.

It is far too early to judge him on this. He put up 54 points in 59 games for the Wild last season, and our talent range for his scoring rate sits well above where he is now; at nine games, the gap is mostly noise. The more useful signal is his ice time, down about three minutes a night from last season, and his five-shot game against Calgary on Nov. 14, which ended with a goal against Dustin Wolf.

Evolving-Hockey rated him 73rd among 401 forwards last season, mostly from even-strength offense. He has always been a passer first, and the players he most resembles in our comparisons are set-up men. The question for Los Angeles is how much of that is left, and nine games can't answer it.
headline: Mats Zuccarello's Kings start has barely begun
